facts.raw_span: numerous whitish papules on the back of more than 10 years' duration
lesions previously resolved with topical corticosteroids but flared soon after treatment discontinuation
some papules became pruritic and extended to the waist and anterior trunk in the past month
no family history of similar lesions was recorded
multiple hypopigmented, flat-topped papules on the back, waist, and inframammary area without genital involvement
most lesions were folliculocentric under close inspection
dermoscopy revealed central keratin plugs and some foci of structureless, whitish, and homogenous areas with surrounding erythema
antinuclear antibody and hyperglobulinemia tests were negative
biopsy specimen from back showed central follicular plug and epidermal atrophy covered by orthokeratotic stratum corneum
papillary dermis was markedly thickened with homogenized collagens, areas of edema, and sparse bandlike lymphocytic infiltration
some eosinophils in infiltrate and red blood cell extravasation
congo red and mucicarmine stains were negative for amyloid and mucin

concepts.why: Folliculocentric papules with central keratin plugs and epidermal atrophy are characteristic of lichen spinulosus.
Multiple hypopigmented, flat-topped papules with folliculocentric distribution are consistent with keratosis pilaris.
Pruritic papules with a history of flare-ups after treatment discontinuation are suggestive of lichen planus.
The presence of pruritic papules with a history of flare-ups after treatment discontinuation, and negative antinuclear antibody tests, could suggest psoriasis.
The combination of folliculocentric papules with central keratin plugs and epidermal atrophy could be indicative of Darier disease.
The presence of multiple hypopigmented, flat-topped papules with folliculocentric distribution could suggest pityriasis rubra pilaris.
The combination of hypopigmented, flat-topped papules with folliculocentric distribution could be indicative of ichthyosis.
The presence of multiple hypopigmented, flat-topped papules with folliculocentric distribution could suggest phrynoderma.
